title: That Night
description:
Rain fell. Beyond the drops gathering on the window, Seoul's lights stretched into long smears.

It was after eleven when someone knocked. Daeun stood outside in her navy convenience-store polo and beige cardigan, a small plastic bag in one hand. The wet ends of her hair clung to her cheek.

"Sorry it's so late."
She started to smile, then stopped. "For some reason, I didn't want to go straight home tonight."

{name} stepped aside and Daeun entered carefully. A bottle of soju and convenience-store snacks tapped together inside the bag. She wiped her wet hair with her cardigan sleeve and looked out the window as if nothing were wrong.

choices.text: Hand her a towel, and do not ask why she came.
choices.result_text:
{name} handed her a towel and sat across from her. He did not ask why she had come or what had happened.

Daeun slowly pressed the towel to her hair. After listening to the rain for a while, she said, "It's strange. I came here to talk, but right now I wanted you not to ask."

"Then I won't."

A little of the tension left her shoulders.

choices.text: "Did something happen?" Ask slowly enough that she can decline.
choices.result_text:
{name} took out the glasses first, making it clear he would not rush her answer. Daeun watched the rain run down the window for a long time.

"Tonight, I didn't want to say I was fine."

It was a short sentence, but from Daeun it sounded like a long confession. {name} only nodded and waited while she chose her next words.

title: What He Did Not Ask
description:
Even after her hair was dry, Daeun kept the towel folded across her knees. The refrigerator motor and rain against the window took turns filling the silence.

"Minjun, sometimes you wait too long for me."
"Do you hate it?"
"No. That's why I end up saying more."

In fragments, Daeun told him about the convenience store: the things a drunk customer had knocked over, another shift change, the words she had swallowed with an untroubled face. None of it was a major incident. That was why it had accumulated for so long.

When her last sentence ended and {name} was still beside her, Daeun let her hands relax on the folded towel.

choices.text: Stay beside her until she is ready to look up.
choices.result_text:
The level in the soju glasses barely changed. Instead, the words between them grew a little lighter.

At last Daeun looked up. "I'm all right now. Not the automatic answer. I mean it."

This time, her eyes stayed on his.

title: A Place Where She Could Be Not Fine
description:
"It was nothing serious."

That was how Daeun began. The words a drunk had thrown at her, the manager changing next week's shifts again, having to smile at home so no one would worry. One by one, the things she called nothing serious came to rest on the table.

"Maybe I'm allowed to say I'm not fine sometimes. When I'm with you."
"You don't have to be fine tonight."

Daeun pressed her lips together and nodded once. Her eyes were wet, but she did not cry. Light blurred by the rain moved slowly across her face.

choices.text: Clear the glasses away and move a little closer instead of answering.
choices.result_text:
When {name} pushed the empty glasses aside, Daeun turned to face him.

"Thank you. Not for fixing it. Just for listening."

Even after the words ended, neither looked away. Their breathing sounded closer than the rain.

title: Before the Light Went Out
description:
Under the low light, the soju glasses went back and forth a couple of times. They laughed, then talked less — until only the rain beyond the window remained.

Daeun looked at {name} for a long moment. She did not put on a smile first or turn her eyes away. Neither did he.

Between two people past thirty, there was a distance that no longer needed explaining. It closed one handspan at a time.

Daeun's fingertips touched the back of his hand. He had expected them to be cold. They were warm, and trembling just slightly.

"...Minjun."

Daeun rested her hand on the light switch and waited.

choices.text: Take that trembling hand in his.
choices.result_text:
{name} took that trembling hand in his. In the dark, Daeun's breath came closer.
The rain filled the world beyond the window — and the rest of that night belonged to the two of them alone.

Morning. He woke as grey light came through the window. Two people lay on the bed.
Daeun was still asleep with her head on his arm, her face undisturbed by a single turn in the night. Her glasses lay beside the pillow where she had taken them off. That one small thing said it plainly: this was no longer a place for one.

Gangnam and three billion won were very far away that morning.
For a man who believed life waited somewhere beyond the target, that morning arrived before the numbers did.

choices.text: "...Just stay next to me tonight." (Falls asleep holding her)
choices.result_text:
{name} held her hand, then pulled the blanket up over her damp shoulders.
"...Let's just stay like this tonight."
Daeun looked startled for a second, then smiled quietly. "...You really are tender in the strangest places, Minjun."

They lay side by side and listened to the rain against the window. Daeun's breathing slowed until she fell asleep against {name}'s shoulder. Somehow, being two people who did not have to hurry felt deeper.

Love in your thirties held firmer precisely because it was not in a rush.

title: The Last Cup
description:
Five years are almost up.

An evening cafe. Across the table, Daeun worried at the paper sleeve around her cold coffee. The same figures had sat on {name}'s phone for days: the price of a ring, the cash he had left, the distance still separating him from Gangnam.

"Minjun, why are you so quiet tonight?"

Instead of answering, {name} slipped a hand into his pocket, then pulled it back out. His fingertips had caught the corner of a small box. Daeun waited with no idea what was there.

choices.text: Turn the phone face down. Ask where she wants to be next year.
choices.result_text:
"Daeun, where do you want to be this time next year?"

She thought for a moment, then let go of the paper sleeve. "Anywhere. Somewhere I open the door and find your shoes beside mine."

She said it like a joke, but her eyes did not leave his after the smile. Beneath the face-down phone, {name} felt the numbers fall quiet.

choices.text: Admit what he was calculating. "The truth is, I'm scared."
choices.result_text:
"About money?"
"About ruining everything. What I have now, and whatever I might have later."

Daeun did not rush to tell him it would be fine. She wrapped both hands around the cold cup instead. "Does a day ever come when everything is ready?"

{name} had no answer. Daeun listened even to that silence.

title: This Time Next Year
description:
The ice in their cups had nearly melted. One of the lights above the counter went dark, and the remaining customers began to leave.

"Minjun."
"Yes?"
"What I said about next year — I meant it."

Daeun did not press him. She did not look like someone trying to force an answer. She simply stayed, as she had for four years, while {name} searched for the words.

Daeun put a hand on the strap of her bag. If she stood now, tonight would end like any other night.

choices.text: Call to her before she stands. "Wait."
choices.result_text:
Daeun's hand stopped on the strap.

"Yes, Minjun?"

She sat back down. This time, the corner of the box did not slip away from his fingertips.

title: The Proposal
description:
Daeun sat down again. The sounds of the cafe seemed to take one step back from the table.

{name}'s thumb pressed against the corner of the box in his pocket. He had hesitated for days. The price of a ring could have been seed money — and for the first time, doing that math made him ashamed.

Across from him sat the person who had endured four years in this cramped city beside him. Whether he reached Gangnam or not, she had stayed.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.

choices.text: Take out the box. "I haven't reached Gangnam yet — but I want to make this promise first."
choices.result_text:
The box opened on the table. Daeun's gaze stopped on the ring. She drew one breath and found no words.

Her hand flew to her mouth. Her eyes reddened in an instant.
"...Idiot. How many times do I have to tell you? Gangnam doesn't matter."
"That's why I'm asking. Even without Gangnam, you were enough for me."

Daeun nodded hard, over and over.

The woman who had handed him a rice ball at a convenience store five years ago was now the person he had promised his life to.
Five years that couldn't be counted in numbers, all fit into one ring on one finger.

choices.text: Put the box away. "Just a little more... when I'm ready." (Not yet)
choices.result_text:
The box spent another night in his pocket.

Daeun seemed to notice, or maybe not.
"Were you going to say something?"
"...No. Let's eat."

When he was ready. Even {name} could not say what 'ready' meant.
Whether Gangnam came first, or she did — he had postponed the answer again.

description_if_known.daeun_first_night:

Across from him sat the person who had endured four years in this cramped city beside him. Whether he reached Gangnam or not, she had stayed.

He remembered that rainy night: her hand before the light went out, the grey light of morning. Perhaps he had already known then that she was the one.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.
description_if_known.daeun_seen_by_gifts:
Daeun sat down again. The sounds of the cafe seemed to take one step back from the table.

{name}'s thumb pressed against the corner of the box in his pocket. He had hesitated for days. The price of a ring could have been seed money — and for the first time, doing that math made him ashamed.

Canned coffee, socks, a scarf. Things that cost very little, yet Daeun had smiled for so long each time. He had never given her anything expensive. Instead, each time, he had truly seen her.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.
